channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: South Africa's used car market hit over $800 million in January sales
item.description: South African used-car sales surged in January 2026, sustaining the recovery seen throughout 2025 and underscoring robust demand across brands and models.

item.title: Zambia cuts interest rate to 13.5% as inflation falls faster than expected
item.description: Zambia has delivered a second straight interest rate cut as the central bank signals stronger confidence in the country’s improving economic outlook. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) reduced the benchmark lending rate by 75 basis points to 13.5% at its February 9–10, 2026 meeting.

item.title: Senegal launches $100 million onshore oil and gas plan after revoking licenses from Inactive operators
item.description: Petrosen, Senegal’s state-owned oil company, is set to launch a $100 million onshore oil and gas exploration campaign this year aimed at discovering crude in the country’s onshore fields, following recent regulatory changes and the revocation of licenses from operators who have done little or no work.

item.title: Congo’s copper exports jump 10% as Chinese firms lead growth
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) increased its copper exports by nearly 10% in 2025, reinforcing its position as the world’s second-largest producer of the industrial metal after Chile.

item.title: Top 10 universities in Southern Africa, according to latest ranking (2026)
item.description: Higher education in Southern Africa is having a defining moment. In the region, the University of Cape Town (UCT) has once again emerged as the region’s top university.

item.title: What Zambia’s 13.5% interest rate means for the economy
item.description: Zambia’s latest interest rate cut has raised an important question among investors, businesses and ordinary citizens alike: what does this shift really mean for the country’s economic direction?

item.title: Kenya weighs gold diversification alongside other African countries as prices hit new highs
item.description: The policy regarding the acquisition or divestiture of gold for the purpose of augmenting federal reserves varies depending on which African market you find yourself in.

item.title: Following massive diplomatic expulsions from Europe, Russia redirects its envoys to Africa
item.description: Russia looks to be increasing its diplomatic and strategic presence in Africa, redirecting envoys from European countries, where many were expelled following the Kremlin's invasion of Ukraine, to new postings on the African continent.

item.title: Africa's largest airline eyes Australian market to complete presence on every continent
item.description: Ethiopian Airlines has unveiled plans to launch flights to Australia in 2028, marking the final step in establishing a presence on every continent.

item.title: Nigeria–Morocco pipeline project powers new vision for Africa’s energy unity
item.description: Africa’s quest for energy security and economic transformation is gaining renewed momentum, with the Nigeria–Morocco Gas Pipeline and the expansion of the West African Gas Pipeline emerging as strategic anchors for continental integration.
